readout_other: Open Field Test; Forced Swimming Test; Tail Suspension Test; body weight; eyelid ptosis score; Nissl staining; hippocampal BDNF immunofluorescence; hippocampal RNA-seq transcriptome (KEGG/GO/PPI analysis); qRT-PCR validation of hub genes (Fn1, C3, Fcgr2b, Lcn2, Itgb2)
direction_notes: The study did not directly measure neuronal excitation/inhibition; LIPUS reversed LPS-induced depressive-like behaviors (reduced immobility in FST/TST, restored locomotion and body weight, reduced eyelid ptosis), restored hippocampal BDNF expression, and partially reversed LPS-induced hippocampal transcriptomic changes (reduced expression of inflammatory hub genes Fn1, C3, Fcgr2b, Lcn2, Itgb2).
safety_notes: Neurons in the CA1 region were arranged in an orderly manner across the control, LPS, and LIPUS groups, without evidence of neuronal loss or structural damage; these findings indicate that under the present experimental conditions, LIPUS did not cause detectable tissue injury in the mouse brain.

exposures.label: LIPUS to the hippocampus in LPS-induced depression model

timing.protocol_description: Pulsed ultrasound was delivered via a conical collimator (total length ~9 mm, upper inner diameter 14 mm, terminal diameter 5 mm) filled with degassed water, coupled to the skull over the hippocampal target under isoflurane anesthesia. In the LIPUS group, mice received daily intraperitoneal LPS injection followed immediately by a 15-minute LIPUS treatment, once daily for 7 consecutive days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: The mice were randomly assigned to three groups: control, LPS, and LIPUS (n = 8). Following previous studies (Amawi et al., 2025; Yin et al., 2023), a depression-like model was established by daily intraperitoneal injection of LPS (1.0 mg/kg) dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at a concentration of 200 μg/ mL for 7 consecutive days.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: The mice were randomly assigned to three groups: control, LPS, and LIPUS (n = 8). source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Pulsed ultrasound signals were generated by a signal generator (ZK-JLCS-8601, Jiangsu, China) and delivered to an ultrasound transducer with a fundamental frequency of 0.8 MHz. The transducer was coupled to a conical collimator filled with degassed water to ensure precise transmission of acoustic energy to the targeted brain region. Mice in the LIPUS group were anesthetized with isoflurane and positioned in a stereotaxic apparatus, with the collimator tip placed directly on the skull over the designated target area. The collimator had a total length of approximately 9 mm, with an upper inner diameter of 14 mm and a terminal diameter of 5 mm at 5 mm from the transducer surface. During sonication, the collimator was filled with deionized and degassed water to facilitate efficient acoustic coupling. The LIPUS parameters were set as follows: pulse repetition frequency of 100 Hz, duty cycle of 50%, stimulation duration of 60 $s ,$ and tone-burst duration of 5 ms (Chang et al., 2020; Yi et al., 2022). Following completion of the intervention protocol, behavioral assessments were performed; the mice were then euthanized, and hippocampal tissue and serum samples were collected for subsequent biochemical analyses.

flags.reason: Methods state a 'stimulation duration of 60 s' per sonication train but also describe a '15 min LIPUS treatment' given daily; the paper does not clarify how the 60 s train relates to the 15 min daily session (e.g. repeated trains), so both durations are noted in protocol_description.
Paper names the device model (ZK-JLCS-8601) and only gives 'Jiangsu, China' as location, not a manufacturer/company name.
No direct measure of neuronal excitation/inhibition (e.g. electrophysiology or immediate-early gene marker) was made; classified as not_assessed.
Control and LPS-only groups received no ultrasound device or sham procedure at all (only injections); classified as no_treatment_control.
